name: Chambers County, AL
findings: Chambers County has 79 nonprofit organizations. 22 of them (28%) list at least one way to get involved in their tax returns or on their websites: membership, volunteering, public events, or civic and political action.
The most common is public events, listed by 16 organizations.
Social and fraternal organizations are the largest group offering opportunities (41% of those with an identified type).
Compared with 10 similar places, Chambers County has about as many organizations offering opportunities per resident.

observations.title: Fewer organizations list membership
observations.text: Per resident, fewer organizations in Chambers County list membership in their tax returns or on their websites than in 10 similar places (about 73% of the typical level).

confidence.text: Based on 20 organizations here; 47% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Does that match what people here experience? Where do people find groups to join now, including outside formal organizations?

observations.title: Religious organizations that list no opportunities
observations.text: 13 religious organizations here list none of the four kinds of opportunity in their tax returns or on their websites. Many may still offer them without describing them there.

confidence.text: Based on 13 organizations here; 47% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: What do religious organizations here do in the community? How do people find out about them?

observations.title: Social and fraternal organizations stand out for public events
observations.text: 6 social and fraternal organizations here list public events, compared with about 3 in similar places of this size.

confidence.text: Based on 6 organizations here; 47% of all organizations here have no identified type.
